title: AI for Corporate Communications and Marketing

questions.question: Why do AI-assisted communication drafts need explicit review controls?
options: Because polished text can hide weak sources, tone risk, or missing approval
Because AI drafts are always ready to publish
Because communication work never involves stakeholders
Because source material should be removed
questions.explanation: Review controls protect source quality, tone, claims, and approval ownership.

questions.question: Which signal is part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: A brand claim needs evidence and approval before publication.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked communications review plan with controls and rationale
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks scenarios and recommends review controls.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: A named approval owner is a key communications control.

questions.question: When should AI-assisted communication require stronger review?
options: When the message has external reach, sensitive content, a brand claim, or an approval gap
Only when no one will read it
Only when it is already approved
questions.explanation: Risk signals decide how much review is needed.

questions.question: What should AI improve in communications work?
options: Drafting speed plus source, tone, and approval discipline
questions.explanation: AI should support quality and review discipline, not bypass it.
